retrieved_synopses: Karlach confronts Gortash after ceremony in WYR.In this dialogue, Karlach is facing the man who sold her to the devil. She hasn't talked to him in 10 years and she's furious for his betrayal. The player can allow Karlach to fight him here, but in most cases they won't.

Karlach has been sent to prison after deciding to attack Gortash while the steelwatcher is present and now has to be recruited again in Wyrm's prison if players get to free her. She is unhappy - she tried to go after him and failed. She's beating herself up inside and that's manifesting itself in anger.

Karlach has a self-dialogue after defeating Ketheric in the Colony. This is also her first chance to reflect on seeing Gortash - she was NOT expecting to see him here. Because the moment right before this is very high-intensity, I wanted this Karlach moment to start low-intensity and ramp up from there.

First meeting with Karlach, future Origin/Companion. She's a fugitive, wounded and hiding from cultists who are hunting for her to drag her back to hell.The dialogue begins with a stream separating the player and Karlach, as she points a crossbow at them when they approach, holding them at bay. She's fierce, defiant, and intense. But friendly and grateful if the player helps. Shouldn't be too angry - she's in a bad situation and doesn't know who to trust, but she's also been in far worse situations. She has a sense of humour about her predicatment, no matter how bad it gets.

context: Karlach has tracked down Lord Enver Gortash immediately after a ceremony in WYR to confront the man who sold her to the Hells ten years ago and allowed Zariel to take her heart. She hasn’t spoken to him in a decade and is burning with betrayal, self-blame, and a readiness to fight — the player can either calm her or let the confrontation turn violent. Gortash is composed and evasive, claiming it was for the “greater good,” surrounded by his Steel Watch bodyguards and already maneuvering deals (even with the player’s companion) to protect his interests. Karlach’s fury is sharpened by recent failure and imprisonment after a prior attempt on Gortash, so her anger is as much grief and shame as it is revenge.
